subject: Acme Payments - Technical deep dive recap (latency/throughput SLOs)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmepay.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Acme Payments - Technical deep dive notes & next steps

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for taking the time today - great conversation. Below is a short recap of what we heard on the call, the high-level goals you confirmed, and proposed next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Key pain points (what you told us)
- Checkout fraud-detection path is latency sensitive: customers abandon checkout when inference latency spikes.
- Peak-hour throughput spikes (end-of-month and promotional bursts) cause queueing and degraded model quality due to batching behavior.
- Compliance/data residency: logs and request metadata must stay in GCP us-west2; SOC 2 evidence required.

Goals / success criteria (you prioritized)
- p95 end-to-end inference latency <= 120 ms for a 256-token request (primary SLO).
- Sustained baseline throughput ~200 req/s with the ability to scale to 800 req/s during bursts.
- Support for a 7B instruction-tuned model with 512-token context and deterministic outputs for reranking.
- Private deployment (VPC) in GCP us-west2 with KMS/HSM integration and audit logs retention for 12 months.

What we'll deliver next (by Wednesday EOD)
- SLO matrix with target metrics and monitoring signals (attached: SLO_Matrix_Acme_20270321.xlsx).
- Deployment topology diagram showing private control plane, VPC peering, and private endpoints (attached: deployment_topology_gcp_us-west2.png).
- Ballpark cost & capacity estimate for Dedicated vs Private deployment (attached: cost_estimate_dedicated.pdf).
- Proposed technical workshop: 60-90 minute session where Vivek and Dev walk through runtime configuration, autoscaling, and canary rollout plan.

Immediate asks for you
- Confirm the p95/p99 latency targets above and whether the 512-token context is the right worst-case.
- Share any compliance docs (SOC 2 scope) or a point of contact for procurement/legal.

Next steps
- I'll send the artifacts mentioned above and propose times for the technical workshop. Vivek and Dev will join to cover runtime/ops.

Thanks - talk soon.

-

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmepay.com>

Subject: Re: Acme Payments - Technical deep dive notes & next steps

Marissa -

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirmations/clarifications below:

- Targets: p95 <= 150 ms is our internal target for now (we measured p95 ~220 ms today). If your testing shows consistent p95 <= 120 ms for 256 tokens that's ideal; we can treat 150 ms as the negotiated target for SLA discussions. p99 target we expect < 300 ms.
- Throughput: baseline 200 req/s is correct; peak bursts can reach 700-900 req/s for short windows (5-20 minutes). We need autoscaling that can handle that ramp without sustained overprovisioning.
- Model: 7B instruction-tuned (open model) is our preferred target. We will also want a smaller fallback (3B) for degraded modes. Determinism matters for reranking.
- Deployment: prefer Private (VPC) in GCP us-west2. SOC 2 is required - I will share our compliance checklist and legal contact (cc'd Tom).
- KMS/HSM: we use Google KMS today; we need to ensure Redwood supports our KMS key lifecycle and HSM-backed keys for encryption at rest.

Please proceed with the artifacts and schedule the workshop - mornings next week (PDT) work best for our infra team.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sr. Engineering Manager, Platform

Subject: Re: Acme Payments - Technical deep dive recap (latency/throughput SLOs)

Hi Sarah / Tom -

Appreciate the confirmations. Below is a technical recap that we will use as the basis for the workshop. This is intentionally detailed so your infra team can validate constraints ahead of the session. I've attached the SLO matrix, topology diagram, and a ballpark cost estimate.

Summary of technical targets (finalized)
- Primary SLOs:
  - p95 end-to-end inference latency <= 150 ms for requests up to 256 tokens (negotiable to 120 ms if testing allows).
  - p99 <= 300 ms.
  - Sustained baseline throughput: 200 req/s. Burstable to 800-900 req/s for short windows (5-20 min).
- Availability target: 99.9% at the route level (we'll discuss contractual SLA in procurement).

Model & runtime guidance
- Model: 7B instruction-tuned model (quantization recommended for cost/latency). We recommend evaluating INT8 or 4-bit quantization with accuracy checks in your eval harness.
- Fallback model: 3B quantized variant for graceful degradation (reduced latency/cost).
- Token budget/contexts: plan for worst-case 512-token context for capacity planning (SLOs measured at 256 tokens; expect ~20-40% higher latency for 512).
- Determinism: Redwood can provide deterministic sampling settings; we'll document seed/temperature controls and ensure the reranking flow keeps determinism.

Latency & throughput engineering notes
- Continuous batching: we recommend conservative batching for user-facing paths; target 5-10 ms batching delay windows and small max batch size to avoid tail latency spikes.
- KV cache: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts in checkout flows to reduce per-request compute.
- Kernel selection: our serving runtime will select int8-friendly kernels for quantized models; expect 1.8-2.5x perf improvement versus FP16 for 7B depending on quantization strategy.
- Recommended instance types (GCP us-west2): NVIDIA A10G or T4 for cost-sensitive workloads; H100/A100 for heavy throughput or larger models. For 7B quantized, A10G usually provides best cost/latency tradeoff.

Autoscaling & deployment topology
- Warm pool: maintain a warm pool sized to cover ~50% of baseline to reduce cold-starts during bursts.
- Scale-out latency: our autoscaler target is to add capacity within ~60-120s depending on instance startup; we recommend a short burstable overprovision reserve (spot-backed or pre-warmed) for immediate spikes.
- Canary rollout plan: 5% traffic for 24 hours monitoring latency, error-rate, and model quality metrics. Rollback criteria: >10% regression in p95 or >2% error increase.
- Fallback policy: route to 3B fallback or reduced-context mode when compute is constrained. We can configure automated routing rules (by route/model) with simple priority-based failover.
- Networking: Private control plane with VPC peering and private endpoints into your GCP project. TLS1.3 in transit, and support for Google KMS/HSM with customer-managed keys.

Observability and SLOs
- We'll instrument token-level latency, per-route p50/p95/p99, queue length, batch sizes, and error rates.
- Alerts: p95 > target for 5 consecutive minutes, or sustained queue growth, will trigger an on-call page.
- Audit logs and retention: configurable to meet your 12-month requirement; we will provide evidence for SOC 2 scopes.

Risks & validation items for the workshop
- Quantization trade-offs: accuracy needs to be validated on your eval set before finalizing int8/4-bit.
- Cold-start behavior for large bursts: need to confirm whether spot-backed pre-warmed capacity is acceptable for cost/ops.
- Network egress and cross-region fallbacks: will confirm routing policies if us-west2 capacity is constrained.

Attachments (included)
- SLO_Matrix_Acme_20270321.xlsx
- deployment_topology_gcp_us-west2.png
- cost_estimate_dedicated.pdf

Proposed next steps
1) Schedule the 60-90min technical workshop - mornings next week (PDT) work for your team. Vivek and Dev will present runtime configs and the autoscaling plan.
2) You share the SOC 2 checklist and procurement contact (Tom).
3) We run a short quantization validation on a 1k-sample eval set (we can coordinate upload of a hashed dataset in the workshop).

If that all looks good I'll circulate calendar invites and the workshop agenda.

Best,
